The strategy-game Magic of Endoria takes place in the fantasy kingdom Endoria. Aeons ago the gods of Endoria were disgusted by the badness in the world and morphed themselves into crystal splinters and retreated into the underworld. Who gets all these splinters becomes the master of Endoria. Now two rival arch mages got aware of this myth and go on the search. You are one of them.

Of course you have to dig deep into the underground to find them. Your responsibility lies in the building. managing and defending of mines. To achieve this you hire employees with different professions: Craftsmen, researchers, mine workers, hauliers and warriors. These people want to see money for their work and they improve their abilities when they become experienced.

During the game you dig new alleys, equip them with traps, research new tools and fight against enemy troops to conquer their alleys. Later you have mutated creatures to your disposal. You spend most of your time on a map with hexagonal fields. There you issue orders and set the routes of your employees.

The in 1995 released CD-ROM version features speech, new background music and an online help. Additionally there is a "light" version of the game which tones down the complexity.

The PC version of Magic Endoria differs from the Commodore 64 version released the previous year in that it is real time instead of turn based.

216966.overview: Mouskattack is very similar to Pac-Man. Take the role of Larry Bain, a plumber working for Rodent Rooter attempting to get rid of all the huge rats in Rat Alley. The player is pursued by 4 rats in a maze and the player must set mousetraps to get rid of them all as well as make sure the player traverses the entire maze à la Pac-Man to complete the level.

419827.overview: When religious artifacts from around the world, often with insignificant market value, start to disappear, Interpol realises it is not the work of a dishonest collector. Clues lead suspicion to fall upon commando and former CIA agent Joachim Wadner, who appears unhelpful but intelligent. To catch the thief, Interpol chooses their best trainee, protagonist and playable character John Pollack, a young American of Polish descent. Pollack has unlimited funds at his disposal, complete a Rubik's Cube in under three minutes, and can kill with his bare hands. He takes his gadget briefcase, boards a submarine, and sails to the Pacific Ocean.[3]

421723.overview: Sometime in 1999, a North American defense network went haywire and caused a nuclear armageddon, forcing the surviving remnants of humanity to move into cramped and unclean underground shelters. A mysterious organization called "New Hope" emerged, promising much better living conditions for joining them, in exchange for many personal freedoms. After an unknown amount of time passes, New Hope creates the space station known as SKYNET CITY, the new capital of humanity. In this city, New Hope has total control, disposing of their opposition and those seen as "no longer useful" to them. You play as Jet Hunter, who takes issue with New Hope's authorities killing his parents (New Hope's top scientists) with no reason or explanation. One day, Jet is contacted by the leader of the resistance against New Hope, named Mars. Mars informs him that something important awaits him and that New Hope has sent a platoon of soldiers after him for his suspicions. Jet arms himself with his trusty Uzi and the game begins.

422786.overview: In this Christian adventure game, you assume the role of Moses, who must free his people, the Israelites, from slavery in Egypt. A text adventure, with optional graphics. Follows the book of Exodus very closely, and the "hint" feature usually directs you to read a particular passage. The game itself is quite short and relatively easy, with much of the important parts of the story presented as several screens of non-interactive text. Many of the early "puzzles" involve addressing places or people by name. Unintentionally funny at times.

424966.overview: Memento Mori (MM.WAD) is a 1995 megawad for Doom 2 that contains 32 new levels, designed by two members of the Innocent Crew, Denis and Thomas Möller, along with 19 other authors, including Tom Mustaine and both Dario and Milo Casali - this made it by far the largest collaborative project up to that point. It was initially released on December 10, 1995, and saw an updated release in February 1996. In contrast to most megawads, it is designed especially for cooperative multiplayer gameplay, although it can be played in single-player as well. It is also one of the few PWADs that are allowed to be used in Compet-N speedruns. The phrase Memento Mori is Latin and is translated as "Remember that you will die" or "Remember death".

424993.overview:
Memento Mori II (MM2.WAD) is a 1996 megawad of Doom 2 that contains 32 new levels, plus two top-secret levels. Released on July 27, 1996, it is the sequel to the 1995 megawad Memento Mori, with many of the same designers involved, including Denis and Thomas Möller of the Innocent Crew. Like its predecessor, and in contrast to most megawads, it is designed especially for cooperative multiplayer gameplay, although it can be played in single-player as well. It is also one of the few PWADs that are allowed to be used in Compet-N speedruns.

In 2003, Memento Mori II was named as one of the Top 100 WADs of All Time, as one of the top 10 WADs of 1996.

428798.overview: After restoring balance and order to the shattered realms in Magic Carpet, you retired to live a peaceful life content in the knowledge that you have saved your people. Your idyll won’t remain peaceful for long, however, as Vissuluth the Dark One emerges from the Netherworld. The Netherworld is a place where demons and lost souls dwell and the Master Demon has grown powerful enough to bridge the great gulf between life and death. The Dark One and his minions threaten the world of men and it is up to you, under the guidance of your old master Kafkar, to once again take up the wizard’s mantle. Prepare to ride the Magic Carpet into terror and danger and emerge victorious!

454726.overview:
The Adventures of Max & Millie is an educational game aimed at children aged 5 to 8. The game combines elements of arcade-style gameplay with learning activities designed to develop mathematical and cognitive skills. Players solve puzzles that focus on recognizing attributes, grouping, sequencing, and continuing patterns.

The game encourages cooperation and teamwork while providing challenges to improve problem-solving and information-processing abilities. Through interactive gameplay, children are introduced to concepts such as working mathematically, understanding space, chance and data, and numbers.

454762.overview:
Metal Slug: Super Vehicle-001 is a run-and-gun action game originally developed by SNK for the Neo Geo platform in 1996. In 1999, a version was released for MS-DOS in South Korea.

In the game, players control soldiers battling against a rebel army, navigating through various missions filled with enemies and obstacles. The gameplay is known for its detailed pixel art, intense action, and cooperative gameplay.

455217.overview:
The appearance of Metal Saver on personal computers was an accident. The game developer, the South Korean company First Amusement, specialized in arcade machines and produced products exclusively for them. And Metal Saver, his third game, was apparently an experiment in moving to other platforms. His success can be judged because this has never happened again.

The game is a platformer with a significant combat component, but it is somewhat unusual: each level is a separate screen with its architecture and opponents. The stage is considered completed as soon as all the enemies are defeated, and it may seem that you can complete Metal Saver quickly and confidently, but we will warn you right away: this is not the case. It's all about the very high difficulty of the battles: even though each defeated foe drops a nice bonus that has a positive effect on the hero's "characteristics", it is not easy to cope with them. Here's what we can expect: large portions of incoming damage, the need to quickly move to a more advantageous position to resist a superior enemy. The lack of any stunned reaction from enemies after a missed hit may shock many fans of the genre. And just one attempt, after which you will have to start all over again...

Theoretically, a co-op in hot seat mode can make the passage easier: you can play in it as a boy or a girl (who can shoot) of your choice, but both simultaneously. In this case, tactical opportunities expand - and victory becomes quite likely, and if not, then at least there will be a friend who will console and support you.

Unfortunately, the game did not reach computers in its entirety and does not contain all levels of the original: this is something like a demo version since a full-fledged commercial release for DOS, alas, never took place. But this does not mean that fans of complex action-oriented platformers and beat-em-ups should bypass Metal Saver. On the contrary, acquaintance with this rare curiosity will enrich their experience, and for other oldgamers, it will be an interesting excursion into the "past that never was."
Review by: Sharp_ey

455340.overview: Improve your spelling and vocabulary skills in this flexible and creative contest of wits. Type in as many words as you can, anywhere on the gameboard, with scrambled letters and wildcards. Multiple definitions and hints are provided, as well as a 65,00 word on-disk dictionary, four levels of difficulty, and an adjustable game timer.

455341.overview:
Create intersecting equations on a crossword style gameboard. Practice math facts (+,-,/,x) at three levels of difficulty and solve challenging word problems. Learn to manipulate numbers and operands, reason deductively, and practice mental estimation skills. It's creative and fun!

1. No two games are ever alike.
2. Solve over 200 challenging word problems.
3. Keep track of wins and losses on unique blender trophies.

Fifteen minutes of digitized speech, whizzing spaceships, exploding cubes, dropping glop and more dot this looney landscape. Funny humor, wisecracking Mutanoid aliens, realistic sound effects, and a playful musical score will delight and instruct the whole family.

455345.overview:
Mad Mac 2 is a 2D platformer in German with six stages. It is the sequel to The Incredible Adventure of Mad Mac.

The people of Kia village have asked Mad Mac for help. An evil spirit is said to occupy the cursed castle of Pautou nearby. Once again Mad Mac has to find keys, navigate mazes and evade enemies to reach and defeat the evil spirit.

455346.overview:
Machine Nation is a vertical-scrolling shoot-'em-up with visuals somewhat similar to Stargoose Warrior, but more focussed on avoiding obstacles rather than on shooting. The objective is to get back to the mothership while flying over a hostile machine city (hence the game title).

One of the features of Machine Nation is that the player's ship can fly at high or low altitude. The latter uses up more fuel but allows to completely avoid enemy attacks. However the player cannot fire back in this mode either. Changing altitude is only possible by flying over specific, marked tiles on the game field.

455354.overview:
Isometric MS-DOS game on CD-ROM, with an installable launcher for Windows 3.1/95.
Max & Sparky is an advertising game created to promote the laundry detergent known as OMO in Finland, Austria, the Netherlands and Denmark, a.k.a. Skip (Portugal, France, Greece, Spain & Germany), a.k.a. Persil (England & Ireland), a.k.a. Via (Sweden).

The game is clearly made primarily for children, which can be seen both in the graphics and the simplicity of the gameplay. The world of the game is declared to be hostile and "dirty", but in fact it is relatively clean, but there are completely non-scary, harmless and non-chasing creatures that must be shot with a water pistol taken at the beginning of the game.

The only difficulty is that they are often extremely difficult to hit, but this is quite solvable: they crawl in a straight line, so after some effort you can "come out" to the same line. By the way, when hit, the creature is not killed - it falls into a soap bubble and flies somewhere up. It is clear that there are bonuses in the form of first aid kits and other things. You can only get hurt by an accidental collision with a creature. But getting into the water in the game is fatal (the action takes place on the islands).

However, all of the above is only the beginning of the game, then it should become more interesting. The graphics are hand-drawn and very pleasing to the eye. The verdict is that the game is really clearly childish, but it is kind, bloodless and entertaining.

456084.overview: A BASIC adaptation of miniature golf for 1 to 10 human players, courtesy of SoftSide magazine. 9 holes are played in sequence, with a top-down view of the course, and each player in turn attempts to complete a hole. A shot is performed by positioning the putter at an angle and selecting a swing force from 1 to 9; each hole has a pre-determined par - the player's number of strokes minus the par determines the score, so (as in standard golf) lower scores are better.

456168.overview: A superb arcade / adventure game where, equipped with a Casquo Laser combination, you have to pass through more than eighty rooms where you will discover different and increasingly powerful weapons without which you cannot progress. of your advance, also put on the combinations that you find because they will protect you against the enemies with the increasing powers. You still wonder why you must take all these risks and perhaps perish ... It is necessary because you must kill the MALOX agent who stole the MEGATRON bomb formula and you want to sell it to an enemy power. It's up to you to discover it while trying to avoid the multitude of traps that you will encounter on your journey.

456437.overview:
More than a compilation, this collection brings three Magnetic Scrolls' hits, now enhanced to run under Wonderland's Magnetic Windows game environment:

Fish!
Corruption
The Guild of Thieves

456670.overview:
MasterType is an educational game that teaches the player how to type with the keyboard. In the game, the MasterType is a powerful wizard who is helping the player defending his command ship by using his laser-like force. The command ship is stationed in the center of the screen and from each corner of the screen, missiles are launched toward the ship. In each corner of the screen, there is a word and by successfully typing in these words the wizard uses his force to zap the missiles. The command ship has four areas and when an area has been hit by a missile, it's shield will be destroyed. If the same area is hit a second time, the whole ship will explode and the game will be over.

The game consists of 17 or 18 lessons depending on the version and is chosen before the game begins. The first lesson deals with the home row keys (a to ;) and the player only has to enter single letters. As the difficulty increases with each lesson, longer and more complex phrases needs to be typed in. Once a lesson is completed, the player gets a summary showing how successful they have been and whether further practice is needed. Some options exist to alter the game after the player's needs. A beginner mode can be turned on and it's also possible to set a speed goal (number of words per minute). In addition to the lessons included, it is also possible for the player to create new lessons.

456687.overview:
Math Blaster Mystery is a junior high school level math and problem solving game for multiple systems.

There are 4 different math challenges, with each containing 4 levels of difficulty:

Decipher the Code - The player must decipher a mathematical equation by trying to fill in blanks. Each turn, every correct number or operation is kept for the next round. The goal is to decipher the algorithm in the minimal number of turns.
Follow the Steps - The player is walked through completing a word problem, by determining which information is important, how to solve the problem, and ultimately producing an answer
Search for Clues - The player searches an old house by selecting the items and people pictured. Each selection will give a clue to the mystery number. When the player has gathered enough evidence, they can solve the problem, with the goal being to use as few clues as possible.

Weigh the Evidence - A Tower of Hanoi based puzzle, where the goal is to place the desired weights on the scale to the far right.

456780.overview:
McGee is an educational game for young children (ages 2 to 6). The game is entirely wordless and tells its story through graphics and sound making it possible for the child to play the game without help from an adult. The idea is that the child in this way should become familiar and confident with the computer and grow a sense of discovery.

In the game the player takes control of a child protagonist called McGee and gets to explore his home. The house consists of a couple of rooms and in each room there are a few objects that can be interacted with. All interaction is done by clicking on the four different icons that appear in each room. When doing so a short animation will start and McGee will do something, for example play with a ball, take a bath or hide under the carpet. There is no specific objective to the game and the player can move around freely between the rooms and interact with things over and over again.

456783.overview: McGee at the Fun Fair is the third game in the McGee series. Like the previous two games it is an educational game for young children that is entirely wordless so that it can be played by the child alone without any help from a parent. The gameplay is identical to the previous games but this time McGee has travelled to a fun fair and along with him comes a friend called Tony. The fair consists of a few different locations and for each there are four icons to click on that cause the two characters to interact with the environment in different ways. This includes watching the various entertainers (a clown, a juggler and a one man band for instance), having fun on the playground and eating ice cream. The game does not have an end sequence so the player can explore the locations freely for any length of time.

457322.overview:
Already a very old, very small, but not losing its charm game at the junction of the racing and sports genres, where we have to control a mountain bike.

There are only twelve "trails", if you can call them that, each of them is limited in time. Our task is to pass them within the set time, adjusting the speed in the course of the ride and pressing the "jump" button when there is some obstacle on the way. Side view in the game.

Obstacles are quite diverse, all are dangerous and include large sharp stones, hills, hummocks, icy areas, and so on. But in the future, some of them will cease to be a threat if we can improve our bike in one way or another, which is done in the "shop" between the tracks. But it is not done for nothing, of course, but for the money that we earn by passing the tracks; The faster they coped with it, the more money they received.

Graphically, the game probably looks simple even for its time, but at the same time it is still very cute, funny, moderately complex, but capable of bringing a lot of pleasure, especially since there are not so many analogues.

P.S.: DOS version of the game is extremely little known and is a rarity.

458031.overview: Very difficult Spanish arcade game. The action occurs in the future, in a kind of extremely hostile and inhospitable world. Milva is most likely the name of the protagonist of the game, a long-haired girl with a blaster that sneaks around this world, which is easiest to describe as “islands inside caves”, making very high jumps and fighting various anthropomorphic and non-anthropomorphic monsters (reptoids with blasters, giant snakes, and so on). Naturally, it is impossible to save game, for each level six lives are given, but after the death of the heroine the game restarts from the very beginning. And she dies here from the slightest contact with the enemies or ammunition of the weapons they use (by the way, her enemies die on single hits too).

458046.overview:
You are Mike Gunner, the most effective detective in the country, who has been hired to end with all the criminals of Robbland city, perhaps the most dangerous city on Earth. You must have very warm nerves, very cold head and especially the most prepared to pull the trigger.

Mike Gunner is a shooting-gallery Operation Wolf-style game, requiring the Gun Stick accessory. The player will have to adjust the contrast and brightness of your screen, in order to gain optimum performance.

Thorough the game you will find people who shouldn't shot at: for example kids or policemen, all of them easily identifiable. But be careful, others will appear disguised as peaceful musicians, and in the least expected moment they will show they are not so friendly.

458209.overview: MISTER GAS is a nice bubble from the upper reaches of the cava, which has been socially reduced to any soda factory by a leak in the piping system. Such humiliation cannot be allowed by the most traveling bubble on this side of MISSISSIPPI. Being reduced from being one of the wealthiest bubbles on the market to being a vulgar component of soda! Being ingested by the jet-set and being able to climb their privileged heads or be swallowed by anyone from the common people, and then simply be expelled! Or worse still be mixed with wine! She! Thought and designed to satisfy the most exquisite palates in the country. To avoid being the laughingstock of his own, he must reach the rusty tap that ends in the proper conduit for his privileged status.

458274.overview: T.M.S. games were incredibly simple: puzzles and classic games reworked so we didn't have to bother opening a box and removing pieces. And Megametropolis, a simple version of Monopoly, was no exception.

458322.overview:
"Mémorise" is a game by Vivian Peshard from the same series as "Associe": this time we don't have to find "pairs" for objects, but simply remember the location of pictures in six cells on the screen (a ball, a boy, mushrooms of different colors, a house, a flower, etc.), and after they disappear from there and start appearing one at a time, indicate where exactly it should be.

It is a multi-language game FR-EN-DE-IT-ES

458323.overview: You play the role of Luis, a boy who has to find a series of things to go to the World Cup in France.

458713.overview:
You control a young boy called Johnny Burger who plans to visit his cousin Emanuel for two weeks. As he arrives he finds him gone. A scientist, who's also looking for Johnny's cousin, comes by and offers Johnny 500DM (Deutsche Mark) for an experiment. Of course, the experiment goes awry. During the procedure a mysterious guy flashes the scientist's memory. The emerging irritation causes the professor to start pushing random buttons, which results in Johnny's transformation as a human pig. After Johnny wakes up the professor is gone, too, as he was kidnapped to the Planet Ladea.

So, Johnny's quest comprises of finding the professor to be transformed back into a normal state and finding out what happened to Emanuel.

Mutation of J.B. plays like a usual Point 'n Click comic adventure. At the bottom of the screen you find a selection of commands in German ("Go to", "Talk to", "Look at", "Use", "Take") and your inventory that stores all collected items. The game doesn't include English subtitles.

459134.overview:
The world cup of Opera gathers the confrontations of the twenty-four teams which participated in Italy '90, besides offering options of pre-world cup, training and demo mode. If we chose the last one, we will see the computer playing all the matches in the same order the FIFA fixed them. The programmers have also distributed the abilities of every team according to the world ranking position they were occupying in that moment.

During the training, our team will practice on the turf all the time we could need. Once done, we will enter in the world cup mode, in which we can load/save game or start the competition. Chosen the teams, we will play (or see) the matches according to the developing of the world cup. Ampler is the fan of possibilities in the pre-world cup mode, since we will play with those teams we would have selected, being them controlled by another player or the computer.

459160.overview: Soccer penalty simulator. The graphics are rather nice, although the palette is only CGA. The player sprites are large, although somewhat caricatural. The first rows of stands with fans are visible on the screen. The game supports single player against AI or two players, but unfortunately are all information about the shot is visible on screen, there's not much challenge for two players.

459489.overview:
A basic fighting game, originally from Spain, which appears to feature 4 combatants and 4 locations.

You have the following attacks:
Standard (Ctrl)
Directional (Ctrl and one of the four cursor keys)
Special (space).

They all work the same for all characters.

One interesting note, is that the more you perform the same attack, the less damage it begins to do over time. This said, you can still easily win a round by just holding the same attack key down.

460120.overview:
Mechanik EN57 is a Polish train simulator released in 1997 for MS-DOS, developed by Aleksander Madej and Robert Kowalski at the University of Łódź. The game recreates the driver’s cab of the EN57 electric multiple unit, a train widely used in Poland since the 1960s. Featuring simple first-person graphics, it stood out for its convincing physics and the ability to customize routes, sounds, and textures.

The DeLuxe Edition (2000) expanded the concept with a dynamic route generator, varied weather conditions, and international scenery. Later, fans created the Trasaland Edition, regarded as the most complete and stable release, adding new routes and improvements.

Despite its technical limitations, Mechanik EN57 is remembered as one of the first cab-view train simulators, pioneering railway immersion on PC, and remains playable today through DOSBox.

460124.overview:
British DMU (Mechanik EN57 Mod) is a fan-made modification created by Steve Green of Trainsimcentral, bringing the Polish train simulator Mechanik EN57 into a British railway setting. The mod replaces the classic EN57 with the iconic British Rail Class 101 DMU, a diesel multiple unit that operated widely across secondary lines in the United Kingdom from the 1950s to the early 2000s.

The modification recreates the Class 101 driver’s cab in a first-person view, retaining Mechanik’s original physics and systems but set within a British route complete with authentic signaling, sounds, and scenery.

Though technically simple, the British DMU Mod is remembered by the community as one of the most creative conversions for Mechanik, expanding the simulator beyond Poland and letting players experience the driving of one of Britain’s most emblematic trains.

460125.overview:
JM2-Mechanik is a fan-made route for Mechanik EN57 created by Iskander, transporting the simulator into a Japanese railway environment. The mod introduces the E231-1000 series EMU, a commuter train widely used on the JR East network around Tokyo since the early 2000s.

The modification goes beyond a simple reskin, featuring a newly designed driver’s cab, custom sounds, and reworked physics, creating a distinctly Japanese driving experience within Mechanik. The scenery reflects Japanese urban and suburban landscapes, complete with authentic signaling and infrastructure, and during the route players can also encounter other E231 units, such as the E231-500 series, adding to the immersion.

With its combination of new assets and improved realism, JM2-Mechanik is regarded as one of the most ambitious and atmospheric conversions of the simulator, allowing fans to experience the daily operation of a modern Japanese EMU.

460127.overview:
McNapoliMechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification created by Iskandar A. W. Mavilio, recreating the Naples Metro Line 1 (Metropolitana di Napoli M1) in Italy. This mod transforms the Polish simulator into an Italian subway environment, with distinctive urban scenery and underground railway infrastructure.

The route places players in the cab of a metro train, adapting Mechanik’s driving systems to the characteristics of a modern rapid-transit line, including steep gradients, station stops, and dense city surroundings. Authentic sounds and visuals evoke the atmosphere of Naples’ underground, offering a fresh experience far removed from the rural and suburban landscapes of the base game.

Widely regarded by fans as one of the most original international adaptations of Mechanik, McNapoliMechanik expands the simulator into the realm of metro operations, capturing the essence of daily commuter service in southern Italy.

460128.overview:
NY-IRT-Mechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification that brings the simulator to the New York City Subway. Based on the historic Interborough Rapid Transit (IRT) system, the mod recreates the experience of operating an R42 subway train, a classic model that once ran on the J and Z lines of New York.

The route features underground and elevated sections, dense urban scenery, and the fast-paced operating style of the NYC subway. The R42 is presented with a dedicated driver’s cab and adapted physics, giving players the challenge of handling tight schedules, frequent stops, and heavy commuter traffic.

With its distinctive atmosphere and metropolitan setting, NY-IRT-Mechanik stands out as one of the most ambitious international conversions of Mechanik, letting players step into the cab of a New York subway train and experience the energy of the world’s most famous rapid transit system.

460129.overview:
emuRoute-Mechanik is a UK-based modification for Mechanik EN57, created by Steve Green of Trainsimcentral, that introduces players to the world of British Rail Class 317 EMUs. The Class 317, first introduced in the early 1980s, was one of the first second-generation electric multiple units in the UK, operating on suburban and regional services around London and the East of England.

This mod recreates the Class 317’s cab in a first-person driving perspective, while adapting Mechanik’s systems to a British EMU environment. The route includes characteristic UK overhead electrification, signals, and scenery, offering a distinct contrast to the Polish railway setting of the original game.

Despite Mechanik’s technical limitations, emuRoute-Mechanik is praised by enthusiasts as a faithful and immersive adaptation, expanding the simulator into British territory and letting players experience the operation of a classic electric unit from the British Rail era.

460157.overview:
PragueMetroMechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification that recreates the first operational section of Prague Metro Line C, running from Florenc to Kačerov. Spanning approximately seven kilometers and featuring nine stations, the route captures the early yet vital stretch of the Czech capital’s subway system.

The mod introduces a modernized 81-71M metro train, complete with a dedicated cab view, adapted physics, and sounds suited for underground operation. Players experience the rhythm of Prague’s rapid transit, with frequent stops, tunnel driving, and authentic urban scenery that reflects the unique atmosphere of the city’s metro.

Regarded as one of the standout international adaptations for Mechanik, PragueMetroMechanik offers a faithful glimpse into the history and operation of the Prague Metro, expanding the simulator beyond its original scope with a richly detailed European subway experience.

460160.overview:
S80-Mechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification that recreates the German S-Bahn S80 line, featuring the ÖBB Class 4020 EMU. The mod allows players to explore an authentic German suburban route, bringing a new cultural and operational setting to the simulator.

Because the project remains incomplete, the cab of the Polish EN57 has been used as a functional substitute. While not an exact representation of the Class 4020’s driving environment, it ensures the route is fully playable and enjoyable until a dedicated 4020 cab can be developed.

Despite this limitation, S80-Mechanik stands out for its faithful recreation of the S80 line and represents a significant expansion of Mechanik into German-speaking railway territory.

460161.overview:
TerraAustralis-Mechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification created by Robert Shaw, set against the vast landscapes of the Australian outback. The route places players in command of a Trans-Australian NR Class locomotive, one of the iconic freight and passenger engines that traverse the continent’s long-distance rail corridors.

The mod emphasizes the sense of scale and isolation unique to Australia’s interior, with expansive desert scenery, long stretches of track, and the operational challenges of running heavy trains across remote terrain. Adapted physics and custom assets help capture the feel of the NR Class in service.

Celebrated as one of the most distinctive international adaptations for Mechanik, TerraAustralis-Mechanik offers players a chance to experience the rugged atmosphere of Australian railroading within the classic simulator.

462383.overview:
In Market Mogul you take the role of Beryl Flinch, company clerk of MegaCorp, headed by the dying president Ebenezer Grimsby, with a job of attempting to save the corporation from a takeover attempt by the executive vice president, Riggs Greedman, Grimsby's rival. From a hidden room filled with direct stock exchange terminals and brokerage house hotlines, and only a starting amount of $25,000, it is your goal to stop Greedman's plans of holding a controlling interest in MegaCorp's 10 subsidiaries, and prevent him from becoming Chairman of the Board.

This turn-based text game displays a list of the different stocks and commodities, along with the current market price, the last change in price, number of shares held, market value of those shares, and total outstanding loans on that stock.

Each cycle, players have the choice of buying and selling your chosen amounts of each stock ('OilCo', 'PowerCo', 'FoodCo', 'ChemCo', etc) and commodities (Wheat, Coffee, Beef, and Gold), along with the option of borrowing against them, where the limit is based on the player's net worth.

After the player is finished setting up their buys/sells and confirming to proceed to the next cycle, the market will update and show the change in each item, along with giving an option to see a trending bar chart of the last 20 market prices for a stock.

Occasionally, there will be 'World event' or market trend that a stock ticker displays (for example: "CABLECO LOSE $5M COPYRIGHT INFRINGEMENT SUIT", or "CHEMCO DEVELOPS STRONG, LIGHTWEIGHT PLASTIC AS STEEL SUBSTITUTE"), and which majorly affects the trend of a specific stock, while some other related stocks may also be slightly affected. Rarely there will also be hints and leaks about upcoming future market trends, true or not.

Once the player holds 1,000 shares of each company, and has a net worth of at least $100,000 for 3 consecutive market updates, the player becomes president of that subsidiary, and starts receiving a 2% salary each cycle for stock held in that company ... but if a stock ever becomes worthless, the player is fired.

The end goal of the game is to become president of all 10 stock companies, and also have a net worth of $250,000, after which the player is elected Chairman of the Board.

The game was a MS-DOS exclusive, originally published in 1983 by Datamost, and re-released in 1986 by Main Street Software.

465752.overview: Il mitico videogame di Mister Fruit Joy is a DOS game in Italian to promote Fruit Joy pastilles (known as Rowntree's Fruit Pastilles in other countries). It is a 2D platformer in which the player must collect a set number of candies to move to the next level. A floppy disk with the game could be obtained by sending in proof of purchase from enough candies.

465770.overview: Houtei Raoyui (a Sino-Japanese term referring to winning a mahjong hand by the last player's discard) is an adult-themed mahjong game. The player assumes the role of a male student in a private high school, where he must compete against seven female opponents in the game of mahjong. The mahjong is always of the one-on-one variety. All the characters except the last one can be selected in any order from the main menu. If an opponent loses a mahjong match the player is rewarded with an erotic picture.

465771.overview:
Manfred Von Krashenbern's Flying Circus is a side-scrolling World War I-themed arcade flight game for DOS.

The player controls a British pilot who must make daring air runs over German lines and engage in dogfights with German pilots. The player starts at the airfield, where they can create a new pilot at the barracks, select a mission, and begin their mission. Missions can include destroying enemy convoys, destroying observation balloons and zeppelins, bombing airfields, and shooting down enemy planes.

Once in flight, the player can steer up or down, reverse direction, loop, fire their guns forwards, or drop a limited number of bombs. Bombs can be used to destroy enemy installations. The screen scrolls in all directions, but a large cliff on the British and German sides of the map prevent the player from flying beyond these boundaries. The player dogfights with German planes, and must avoid anti-aircraft fire while bombing enemy land targets. If the player crashes behind enemy lines that character is lost. A successful mission and landing awards bonus points and potentially medals.

465772.overview: Bowser, the token bad guy from the Mario Bros. series, is up to no good again in this educational game designed to teach children geography. This time he's set up his headquarters in Antarctica and created portals to 25 famous cities around the world, so that his Koopas can wreak havoc in our own world. He's also kidnapped Mario, hence the title of this game. You play as Luigi who must foil Bowser's plans by entering through each of the portals, tracking down the Koopas who have stolen famous artifacts, and looking for clues about your location. Once you've set everything right and determined where you are, you call Yoshi on your Globulator so he can track you down. You need Yoshi's help to eat the Pokey (a cactus-like creature) that's guarding the return portal, and when Luigi returns he can close the portal forever.

465773.overview:
It's the 22nd century, and mankind's greed finds new outlets throughout the Solar system; you, a gem prospector, have set off for the asteroid belt to harvest precious stones. However, an ideological dispute is getting in the way: the Commie Claim Jumpers - a contrary bunch of space pirates - seem to be contesting your mining rights, and voicing their protest by shooting at you and stealing your gems.

This stands a good chance of ruining your day, but you're packing some firepower yourself - your ship's frontal gun, with its limited (but recharging) ammo. Your job is to roam the asteroid field, pick up gems and deposit them at your base for safekeeping. The Marxist marauders come in a variety of vehicles: the Gem Protector and the Seek & Destroy, which fire at you; the faster Kamikaze, which tries to ram you; and the Gem Thief, which lives up to its name by snatching your valued bounty and retreating to its own base. If it's destroyed in mid-thieving, it drops its cargo for you to recover.

465774.overview: As a fly trapped in a maze, you run through the passageways, picking up the numbers that answer the math problems posed at the bottom of the screen. This game leads to some very fast action, especially with the spider, who will chase you down and kill you. This game allows for the players to design their own maze.

465776.overview:
Math Rescue Plus is an expansion pack to Math Rescue, featuring 45 new levels, additional word problems and three different music tracks. There are no changes to the graphics or storyline.

It is a standalone game that does not require the original title to play.

465777.overview: Mathology is an exciting arcade-action math adventure where you flip, jump, duck, move, and shoot your way to victory! But beware of the dangers that abound. Only the warrior will defeat Apathy and return triumphant to Mt. Olympus and Zeus' Chamber. Become part of a Greek legend, learn the "Numbers of Light," and save Greecia forever.

465787.overview:
Maths and English with Rayman: Volume 2 for ages seven and up is the second in a series of educational single player games that uses the platform character Rayman to teach basic numeracy and literary skills.

The games are based around a typical arcade game story. Mister Dark has stolen the contents of the 'Magic Book of Knowledge' and the wise old wizard and Betilla the fairy have called on Rayman to recover it. To do this Rayman must recover twelve golden rings, six grammar related and six maths related. To retrieve a golden ring Rayman must complete what the game calls an activity. Each activity has five stages and the game is automatically saved at the end of stages two, four and the final optional bonus stage which is timed. Progress through the game is shown on the 'Map of the Worlds'. As the player completes the fourth stage of an activity, new paths open up on this map allowing the player to tackle other activities. At the end of the game, when the player has reached Mr. Dark's hideout and retrieved the 'Magic Book of Knowledge' the game ends with a video sequence and presents the player with a diploma that can be printed

465788.overview: Maths and English with Rayman: Volume 1 for ages six and up is the first in a series of educational single player games that uses the platform character Rayman to teach basic numeracy and literary skills.

465789.overview: Maths and English with Rayman: Volume 3 is an edutainment title for ages eight and up that uses the game character Rayman to teach basic numeracy and literary skills. The games in this package are the same as Maths and English with Rayman: Volume 2 but the questions are more difficult to reflect the target age group.

465790.overview:
Mega Maze is a video game approach to the real-life games where you would turn a platform of a maze with a metal ball to miss the holes and reach the middle with a few twists. You control a steel ball, being chased by enemies balls who can destroy you by blowing up when they touch you.

You also have to avoid explosive traps, trap doors and electric sensors. You can even make dummy balls to attract the enemy balls or use them to set on a switch to keep weight on it, giving you time to get through a trap without being caught. It features 75 levels, each with either with one maze clear up to three mazes.

465791.overview: MER Adventure is an advertisement game where the player controls a free climber and the aim is to reach the top of Mt. Guano. Climbing is done by the player by clicking one one of the climbers four extremities, hold in the mouse button and move selected extremities to a suitable crack in the rock wall. At the bottom of the screen two meters can be found: one for energy and one for fatigue. Fatigue is best keeping low by always keep both feet and hands in cracks not too far apart. Energy can be replenished by drinking MER that can be found on cliff shelves here and there.

465792.overview: BBC Radio 1 DJ Mike Read presented a pop music quiz show, which is recreated here with questions from the 50s to the 80s. You can play against the computer or another human; either way, select a specialist subject and 2 team-mate graphics (all representing white people). The overall style and presentation are very similar to Elite's earlier A Question of Sport license.

465793.overview: Muscle Pete's Spell-Off involves the player controlling the titular Muscle Pete. Your task is to spell out the objects that are displayed on the screen. This is accomplished by walking across the floor and touching letters that are above Pete. The game is designed as a way to teach children Spelling 101.

465794.overview:
My Math Tutor is an educational game feature three programs on one disk:1. Exponents Part I: This is the first of two programs designed to teach exponents. This part covers the multiplication of exponents. The program explains various concepts and then presents a various questions on the topics that were covered. Points are earned for providing correct answers.

Exponents Part II: This is the second program which teaches about exponents. It is similar to the first part except it covers division of exponents. The programs presents various concepts and then asks mathematical questions related to the concepts that are covered.

Mental Math: This program is designed to help practice addition and subtraction skills. The program presents a series of numbers one at a time; the goal is to add and subtract the numbers provided and provide the result at the end. Several skill levels are available; the easier skill levels use smaller numbers and provide more time to answer the question while difficult skill levels provide less time or have higher numbers.

465795.overview:
My Own Stories is an adaptation of Storybook Weaver - the educational game/application that allows children of 8 to 14 years of age to write their own stories. Now those stories are based not on fairy tales, but on everyday contemporary situations.

The objects present as possible illustrations for stories depict real life experiences: city, town, school, gym, sports, beach, backyard etc. Change sizes and colors of the objects put on pages is also possible, as well as adding music and sound effects and printing all the results.

466105.overview:
The first role-playing game from Mirinae Software, which had previously created mainly various arcade games (including the scrolling shooter series The Day).

The background of the plot is as follows: Hong Gildong, a character in a literary work of the XVI-XVII centuries, settled on an isolated island of the land of Yuldo, successfully ruled and passed the throne to his son Seong Dogun, who gave birth to the crown prince. The latter, studying under the guidance of his mentor Bupjung, grew up with the son of one of the ministers, Park Joongmoon, and Han Mihong, the daughter of noble parents. Later, Jungmun went to study, and the prince and Mihon became engaged. Everything changed one day when someone named Jeokdae Ma'in attacked the royal palace and occupied the country. The crown prince disappeared, and Song Do-gun and Pubjun were banished to a desert island. A few months later, Jungmun returns to Yurdo, and Song Do-gun dies. Pubjun follows his master's last order and returns to the lands terrorized by Chogdae Ma'in in search of the lost prince. However, the playable characters are Yu Jin Sun and Hong Seyong. The latter has lost his memory, and the former decides to help regain it.

The gameplay resembles console jRPGs, although the locations are interconnected, and there is no division into separate locations and a global map. Dialogues with NPCs are optional, as they do not contain important information for progressing through the story. Skirmishes with enemies are random, and the combat system is semi-turn-based and reminiscent of ATB (Active Time Battle) from Final Fantasy IV: there is a gauge that is constantly filling up, and the character is able to perform one or another action when it reaches the minimum mark. This gives interesting opportunities for tactics: you can deliver quick but weak blows - or, after waiting a little longer, make one, but strong. For winning, you get money, experience and - sometimes - items.

Stats that are varieties of habitual strength, defense, agility, and so on, increase automatically as you level up. Some of the opponents are made either with an eye to folklore, or are characteristic of East Asian games with a national flavor - such as living idols, soldiers in appropriate uniforms, mythological creatures; The latter will meet more than once in the form of bosses. The interface is iconic, so knowledge of the language is not required in battles.

The graphics in the projection with a top view are made at a good level and are pleasing to the eye; It is worth noting the visual unity of the style of different objects and graphic elements. The music also sounds good, although it can get boring due to frequent random skirmishes.

In general, it is a well-made representative of the genre that is interesting to play. Fortunately, thanks to the fan translation into English, much more people will potentially be able to get acquainted with this thing than with the average South Korean RPG.
Review by: Gamerun

466717.overview: Humanity is in an intergalactic war with hostile aliens. You command a ship that, after a space battle, boards the alien mothership. Inside, you can fly or walk through the MadSpace where the laws of physics at times don't apply. There are some pre-rendered interactive sections and cutscenes viewable in Stereo3D. There are 25 levels plus secret areas, with 16 enemy types and 11 extraterrestrial weapons. Up to 16 players can play over a network or through a modem. It also uses speech recognition in gameplay.

467297.overview:
A slightly strange product from a small Taiwanese developer Jack Bean Studio. This studio is known for its very good RPG games that have been released since 1993. But, apparently, in 1995, the creative forces of this team of developers sharply declined. As a result, judging by the intro, we see a clear swing at another good RPG, and in the gameplay we see... Banal Tetris, albeit with a few advanced innovations...

The plot of Tetris is something that only Taiwanese developers are capable of! Well, they clearly conceived an RPG, but something didn't work out for them, and they were just too lazy to remove the story opening animation. It was like this. In one Happy Kingdom (快樂王國), there was a princess (公主). One night during the full moon, she was attracted by the beautiful reflections of the moon on the surface of the royal pool, and she came up to take a closer look... The princess was never seen again, except for frozen puddles of water, one of which was imprinted with hieroglyphs that read about the Ice Queen of the North Country (北國 冰雪女王). The old king was grief-stricken, but he couldn't save his daughter because the forces against the Ice Queen were too unequal. Things changed when a little boy, Xiao Ke (小克), appeared. The king called him specifically so that he could help find a secret weapon on the old map: a powerful bow and arrows, as well as cannonballs filled with magical powers. And so, little Xiao Ke set off... How does this relate to Tetris? – try to think it out yourself.

The passage of the logical game, dressed in the plot outline of an RPG, is as follows. You will complete Tetris levels, and in the story, each of your victories will mean either getting some target items or defeating the Ice Queen. At the end of the gameplay, Xiao Ke and the princess riding a war gorilla (?!) will break into the evil queen's palace and win, and so will you. This is such an unusual course of gameplay.

Tetris is quite unusual. Here, in addition to the passive elements of the "blocks", there are elements of the "food" and "devourer" types. Food, depending on the design of the level, can be represented by berries, carrots, frogs, mice. And the devourer, accordingly, will be a snail, a rabbit, a red ball with an arrow, a cat. The soul of the eaten creature is comically depicted rising with the help of wings upwards – i.e. to paradise. When the blocks line up in one horizontal line with no voids, the line disappears, which is in line with the basic concept of Tetris. There are even exploding objects. Food falling from above constantly tends to get clogged between the blocks. Rarely does a devourer fall with food or blocks, and then wherever he manages to run, the food will be eaten, and the blocks will fall and rarely even line up in horizontal lines. It is impossible for the devourer not to eat someone, then he simply breaks.

467490.overview:
Mortal Pong is a one or two player game that can be played either by two players on the same machine or over a modem via XBAND PC.

The game is based on Pong. Balls are launched from the centre of the screen and the players use paddles to keep the ball in play. The longer the game goes on the more balls appear. If a player lets a ball go past them then they lose health, (the developer says this is similar to a player losing health in the Mortal Kombat games - hence the name), and once a player has lost all health the game is over

468762.overview:
Go Simulator is a computer adaptation of the classic Chinese strategic board game known worldwide as go.

The game includes a complete tutorial to learn the basic rules of go. Using the numerous available options, the player can customize the game to adapt the difficulty: size of the board (from 9x9 to 19x19 lines), AI level (1 to 20), handicap (0 to 29 stones on the board before the game starts), etc. It is possible to play against the computer or a friend, and even watch the AI play against itself.

469624.overview: Mie is a one-on-one fighting game. The protagonist attempts to break into a castle to rescue a heroine. The game consists of five levels (fights) and some small games are interspersed between them, such as a sliding puzzle. There is no save function. The character can fight using a range of attacks. The health meters for both characters are shown in the bottom left corner.

469931.overview:
Minotavrs is the "holy simplicity" of computer games, the genre of which is very difficult to define. Probably, this is not even a rogue-like, but the most top-down-action, but very different from all the usual ones. The only known slightly (a little!) similar thing is the Master of Magic game from Mastertronic for the C64 platform. The game formally has a plot - the hero must defeat an evil vampire - but this is far from the main thing here.

The point of the game is to wander through dungeons and kill creatures. To do this, you need to collect some bottles with, apparently, magic potions - this is what is a weapon against monsters here; Moreover, the same bottle can successfully act on one type of monster and be useless when meeting another.

The game screen is divided into three parts. In the left there is a black square and small dots in it. One of these points is your hero, the others are monsters, various potions and other objects, here you can also mark the walls of the labyrinth that are already "known" (that is, which the hero has encountered); movement in the game is discrete. On the right side, at first, it is generally dark and empty, but when you meet or collide with someone or something, its graphic display appears (a door, a portrait of a monster, a wall, and so on). At the bottom, there is a panel with the current inventory, with which you can choose potions to use.

The battles are quite primitive - when meeting a monster, the hero's life energy begins to decrease, the monster will die the faster the sooner the right object is chosen to destroy it (although the potion may not work on someone for a long time). To move to the next level, you need to find the key to the doors; The levels appear to be randomly generated, but are always quite simple and very similar to each other.

No storylines and other things - only the most "high". As mentioned above, the graphics are practically non-existent. Images of doors and portraits of monsters are made in the CGA palette, but at the same time very clearly and quite beautifully. The result was summed up at the very beginning - despite the simplicity in all respects, this game (a rarity, by the way) is able to insanely captivate and awakens just incredible nostalgia for the good old days.

471080.overview:
The simplest arcade scroller from Taiwanese manufacturers. But, despite the fact that it is the simplest, it will be quite difficult to pass it even at the very beginning of the game. The game is most likely ported from the console, and it is best to use a joystick to control it.

The plot is simple to the point of ugliness. In deep space, the ship of the Earth fleet was attacked by some forces. The red-haired girl commanded you: "MH28, get ready to fight. Your task is to reach the command post near the Daken Star (達肯星)." At this point, the intro with a plot explanation suddenly ends and the gameplay begins. There is nothing in the menu itself, no items - any click takes you directly into the game, which looks extremely simple.

Your boat is made in the form of a small rounded ribbed "seed" of green color. The scroller moves from top to bottom. There are various types of enemy ships: simple, shooting down or firing aimed missiles, and there are also those moving chaotically and striving to "board" you at the first opportunity. MH-28 has the ability to attack with different types of shots (use the "Caps Lock" key to fire). You can also pick up power-ups flying from above. Any contact with enemy ships results in the loss of MH28. However, you are given as many as 9 MH28 warships - this really speaks of the difficulty of the passage. If you lose any of the "lives", the next one will start from the very beginning of the current stage. The graphics are bright, but do not particularly shine with the finest details. Although the game is considered to be made in Chinese, the gameplay does not have hieroglyphs, not even letters, so it will be quite easy for an unprepared (in terms of language) player to get used to the controls, but it will be very difficult to pass this game creation.

471616.overview:
An interesting, but at the same time practically unknown in the West Korean beat-em'up, dedicated to the battles of giant robots among themselves. The game is mostly in Korean (although the menus and a number of interface labels are in English); The background, apparently, is told in the introductory video, but a person who does not speak the language will not be able to understand anything there. However, the plot in such a game cannot be a very important component. Before the start of the game, you can choose a hero - one of two different robots.

The most interesting thing about Mechanic War is that a significant part of the battles between robots (especially at the beginning of the game) take place under physical contact, meaning they fight with various types of melee weapons of enormous size. There are basic weapons (for example, a small drill), and there are those that can be picked up from defeated opponents and "put on" to the mechanical arms of the robot (while other non-basic weapons that are already there will have to be removed). Weapons of this kind include clubs, huge drills, swords-likeness, and so on.

After some time, enemies with ranged weapons will appear, including not only anthropomorphic robots, but also tanks. After the destruction of the latter, the caterpillar base of the tank does not explode, and our robot can climb on it and become one with it, which is very good (especially considering that some tanks in the game are equipped with a powerful laser beam [which for some reason is not emitted from its turret, which we are just destroying]). Side view in the game, but with the ability to move "into the depth" of the screen. Each location usually consists of a single screen, but with scrolling. The pace of the game is comparatively slow for the subgenre.

Separately, I would like to note the wonderful graphics, and first of all, the image quality not even of the backgrounds, but of the robots, which look simply incomparable; The game also has very beautiful explosion effects. Mechanic War is a wonderful example of a really interesting "oriental" game that deserves much more popularity and fame in the world than it received due to its "isolation", but now there is nothing to prevent players around the world from enjoying it to the fullest.

472779.overview:
There is little information about this South Korean platformer, and there are no reviews or videos at all - and this, unfortunately, is quite understandable, since its creators frankly overdid it with the complexity of the gameplay. The plot fits in one sentence: a boy, playing on a console, found himself in the surreal world of video games and now must get out of it. The action itself is preceded by a very long non-interactive dialogue with the sentient mushroom (fortunately, it is allowed to skip it by pressing "Escape").

The perspective of the view is a side view. The hero can jump ("Ctrl") and crouch ("bottom" cursor arrow); "Alt" is responsible for self-defense against enemies, of which there are many. There are several "lives" and a certain amount of health within each of them, but neither the first nor the second is displayed on the screen; Actually, there are no usual indicators on it at all. By default, the boy can throw wrenches; If they suddenly run out (and we again do not know this in advance, since we do not see their reserve), then formally he will be able to defend himself with his fists - but in fact it is unlikely that it will be possible to defeat someone in this way. Obtaining alternative methods of attack is extremely unintuitive: for example, in order to find "launchable" balls that roll on the surface (and at the same time obey some laws of physics, so it is pointless to use them on small ledges), you need to get to the first "terminal". At the same time, no switching between weapons seems to be provided: in different situations, one type or another is arbitrarily used.

The platform element is present, but the main difficulty is not it at all, but the battles: the concentration of enemies is quite high, and sometimes they show true miracles of intelligence. For example, almost at the very beginning, we meet intelligent big-eyed onions on legs: these monstrously aggressive "comrades" not only actively pursue the hero, but also know how to jump perfectly, as well as strive to impose a close fight on him, in which he has no chance against them; The use of wrenches in this case is useless: if the onion comes up to you, then the boy, for some unknown reason, will still throw this object, and not at it, but "into the distance"!! Plus, there are evil workers armed with the same throwing wrenches and able to "pull" their helmets on themselves for a while, almost completely ending up inside their hats (which makes them invulnerable), thick cauldron-shaped robots, creepy chickens, and so on, as well as many basically indestructible enemies and dangers: spiders hanging from above, predatory plants, sharp spikes, and the like. From the point of view of mechanics, the main problem is a very small amount of space for maneuvers: we always seem to be "squeezed" between various structural elements, so you won't be able to jump "to your heart's content", and the passage turns out to be very slow, viscous and exhausting.

474366.overview:
Math Assault II: Fractions is a shareware, educational game that teaches fractions, decimals, ratios, proportions, and percentages to grades 4 - 9.

The game follows on from Math Assault 1. The year is now 2135 and the player, a super hero, responds to a message from Dr. Ronan, an evil super genius who has developed a machine that will enable him to take over the world. While investigating the warehouse that is Ronan's lair our hero is zapped by a green laser and winds up back in ancient Greecia. Things are not well in the past either. Dark magic has forced Zeus from Olympus and he now lives in a cave with Iris his assistant. The only hope is a portal on the far side of Greecia built by the Mooglish but it's guarded by a dragon.

The gameplay that follows is similar to a side scrolling arcade game. The player explores the level killing baddies. When a baddie has been killed the player must answer a math question to earn health and weapon points. Along the way there are power ups to collect, these appear as potions in a window on the right of the play area. There are also gems to collect, these earn bonus points and they explain math terms such as denominator and improper fraction to the player, some of these terms feature in later questions posed by the game. When enough points have been accumulated the player increases in rank and battles the end of level monster. There are eight levels the last of which is the fight with the green dragon that gives access to the portal which takes the hero home.

The game has optional sound, music and speech, a choice of character, play and a practice modes, save game function, two levels of difficulty and a high score table.

474384.overview:
Math Assault I: Word Problems is a one or two player, shareware, educational title for grade levels 2 - 7.

The story behind the game is that the country of Greecia is a place where people live in darkness. Their land has been controlled by a god called Apathy for thousands of years. Zeus planned the downfall of Apathy by teaching the people the wisdom of numbers, this made them strong and they were able to overthrow the evil god and his minions and imprison them. Now, a century later, the people have forgotten Zeus' teachings. Apathy and his crew are out of prison and the only hope for the future is a legendary warrior who will master the world of numbers and destroy all evil in the world.

The game is played in two parts. In the Chamber of Numbers the player must answer a series of math questions which are expressed in words rather than in symbols, hence the name Math Assault I: Word Problems. So instead of being asked, say, 2+2=? The player is given a question like 'Apollo has 2 goats and Zeus gives him 2 more, how many goats does Apollo now have?' By answering correctly and quickly the player gains health points, weapons points, and possibly some of Zeus' bonus points. When the player has answered enough questions correctly they advance in rank and are allowed into the combat part of the game.

The combat part of the game is a two dimensional, scrolling, platform game in which the player must defeat each one of Apathy's minions until, on the eighth level, they defeat Apathy himself on Mount Olympus.

There are three levels of difficulty, a choice of six warriors - three male and three female, optional sound, a save game option and re-definable action keys. The developers claim the game will take between thirty and eighty hours to complete.

475251.overview: A MS-DOS game published by Mindscape and released in 1994 that featured six different winter events - Downhill Slalom, Giant Slalom, Ski Jump, Snowboard Slalom, and Bobsledding.

482712.overview: A science-fiction real-time strategy game featuring armies of giant combat machines. Assemble units from different components to prepare weapons for particular situations. Resource management and army development accompany tactical control of battles throughout the campaign.

482714.overview: After androids take control of Earth, a surviving group of humans seeks alien technology on the distant moon Quadam. As a member of the expedition, explore locations, talk to their inhabitants and use collected objects to overcome obstacles. This Czech science-fiction adventure is controlled with the mouse.
